learnings.question: Which economist and cognitive scientist argued, in a 1971 essay, that an information-rich world inevitably creates a scarcity of a different resource?
learnings.learning: Herbert Simon observed in 1971 that an information-rich world necessarily creates a scarcity of attention, since information itself consumes the attention of whoever receives it.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: In Islamic terminology, what does the Arabic word 'Lagw' — something the Quran instructs believers to turn away from — refer to?
options: Ill or idle speech, such as gossip and meaningless talk
learnings.learning: Surah Al-Mu'minoon (23:1-3) describes successful believers as those who turn away from 'Lagw' — ill or idle speech like drama and gossip that drains attention without adding value.
learnings.articleTitle: Everybody wants your attention, but not everything deserves it.

learnings.question: Which 19th-century psychologist demonstrated that people forget roughly 80% of newly learned material within 24 hours unless they actively work to recall it?
learnings.learning: Back in the 1880s, Hermann Ebbinghaus showed that we forget about 80% of what we learn within a day unless we actively force ourselves to recall it — simply re-reading material doesn't work nearly as well as being quizzed on it.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: According to a hadith recorded in Sahih Muslim, which three things continue to benefit a person even after they die?
options: Wealth, family, and a good name
Ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge, and a righteous child who prays for them
learnings.learning: A hadith in Sahih Muslim (1631) states that when a person dies, all their deeds end except three: ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge they left behind, and a righteous child who prays for them.
learnings.articleTitle: Is Your Brain the Worst Place to Store Ideas? Why I Built a Second One

learnings.question: In agile software development, what is the standard template used to write a User Story in the Product Backlog?
options: As a [role], I want [feature], and prioritize [impact]
As a [role], I need [feature], so that [reason]
learnings.learning: A Scrum User Story follows a fixed template — 'As a [role], I need [feature], so that [reason]' — which keeps every backlog item tied to a role, a feature, and a reason.

learnings.question: In the Scrum framework, during which ceremony does the team demonstrate completed work to the Product Owner and reflect on improvements for future Sprints?
learnings.learning: The Sprint Review is the ceremony where the Scrum team demonstrates completed work to the Product Owner and discusses what could be improved in future Sprints.

learnings.question: Life's purpose in Islamic theology is often described as revolving around three roles. Which set of three correctly captures them?
options: Seeking wealth, building a family legacy, and pursuing worldly knowledge
Following rituals, avoiding sin, and seeking paradise alone
Worshiping Allah, serving as steward (khalifah) of the Earth, and preparing for the Hereafter through accountability
learnings.learning: Islamic teaching frames life's purpose around three roles: worshiping Allah, serving as khalifah (steward) of the Earth, and living as a test of faith where every choice is accounted for in preparation for the Hereafter.

learnings.question: What Arabic term refers to the mindfulness or awareness of Allah's presence that builds self-restraint and purifies a person's intentions?
learnings.learning: Taqwa is the mindfulness of Allah's presence that worship is meant to foster — it builds self-restraint and purifies intentions, steering a person away from wrongdoing.

learnings.question: What did Prophet Muhammad say would succeed him as leaders, instead of future prophets?
options: Scholars only, with no formal leadership
learnings.learning: The Prophet Muhammad said there would be no prophet after him — instead, caliphs (khalifah) would follow as successive leaders responsible for preserving the faith and community unity.

learnings.question: In PCIe power management, which low-power state acts as a very light sleep, letting the link quickly resume activity, meant for only very short periods of idleness?
learnings.learning: L0s is PCIe's lightest power-saving state — comparable to a computer screen turning off — designed for brief idle periods where the link needs to wake up almost instantly.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: Which PCIe power state is comparable to a computer being completely shut down — offering the greatest power savings but taking the longest time to resume activity?
learnings.learning: L2 is PCIe's deepest power state, almost completely powering down the device — it delivers the highest power savings of all the states but also has the longest wake-up time.
learnings.articleTitle: Power Management States in the context of PCIe

learnings.question: In Islamic theology, what is the key difference between 'Qada'' and 'Qadr'?
options: Qada' is the actual unfolding of events in life, while Qadr is Allah's complete, eternal, pre-written plan
Qada' is prayer while Qadr is fasting
Qada' is destiny while Qadr is simply free will with no plan
They are two different names for the exact same concept
learnings.learning: Qada' refers to the events that actually occur in a person's life, shaped by their choices, while Qadr is Allah's complete and eternal knowledge of everything that will ever happen — including those very choices.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: In Islamic teaching on supplication (Dua), what does Allah guarantee when a Muslim sincerely calls on Him for something that isn't sinful and doesn't sever family ties?
options: Allah only grants it during the last third of the night
Allah only grants it if it's repeated exactly 100 times
Allah grants it, or wards off a similar evil from them
learnings.learning: A hadith in Jami at-Tirmidhi states that Allah responds to every sincere Dua that isn't for something sinful or for severing family ties — either granting it directly or warding off a similar evil in its place.
learnings.articleTitle: The Art of Qada’ and Qadr

learnings.question: When a data analysis counted every word's frequency across the Arabic text of the Quran, what share of the entire Quran did just the top 20 most frequent words actually make up?
learnings.learning: Despite the Pareto principle's usual 80/20 split, a word-frequency analysis of the Quran found that its top 20 most frequent words only account for about 20.83% of the total text.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python

learnings.question: Which short, repeated Quranic phrase — asking which of the Lord's favors will be denied — turned up as one of the most frequently repeated verses in a word-frequency analysis of the Quran?
options: "And your Lord is most forgiving, full of grace"
"Allah is sufficient as a disposer of affairs"
"Then which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?"
learnings.learning: A data analysis of repeated verses in the Quran found "Then which of the favors of your Lord will you deny?" (from Surah Ar-Rahman) among the most frequently repeated phrases in the entire text.
learnings.articleTitle: Top 20 Words to Understand the Quran: A Data Analysis using Python
